# SCARE: A Benchmark for SQL Correction and Question Answerability Classification for Reliable EHR Question Answering

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#scare)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlresearch/v297/main/assets/lee26b/lee26b.pdf) · ML4H 2025 manuscript in PMLR volume 297; catalog correctly separates conference year from 2026 proceedings record

**Reading coverage:** All twenty-one PDF pages, Sections 1-7 and Appendices A-F, full model tables, annotation protocol, error taxonomy and baseline prompts.

## Research question

A post-generation component must preserve valid SQL, repair erroneous SQL and identify ambiguous or unsupported questions.

## Method

SCARE balances four categories across three EHR schemas, using candidate SQL from seven generators. Ambiguous/unanswerable questions are model-generated and independently checked by three SQL-proficient annotators. Baselines combine classification, SQL correction, verification and self-refinement.

## Evaluation

The 4,200 triples are evenly distributed across databases and categories. Preservation and correction rates include all examples in their category, so false refusal is penalized. Ambiguity/refusal use per-class classification metrics. Several baseline prompts also include execution results and annotation evidence.

## What the results support

The main Gemini-2.5-Flash experiments expose preservation-versus-detection trade-offs and weak handling of vague questions/global SQL errors. Appendix A shows substantial backbone-dependent variation; the main-table ambiguity maximum is not the maximum across all tested models.

## Limits and qualifications

Balanced diagnostic cases do not represent clinical query prevalence. Academic/demo schemas and single-response judgments do not establish production safety or successful clarification. The proposed pre-execution framing should not be confused with execution-free baseline inputs.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Directly evaluates the interaction between request answerability and candidate SQL correctness, while keeping them separate.
